name: Germanic New Medicine

card.summary: A belief system created by Ryke Geerd Hamer that attributes illness to unresolved emotional conflicts; followers apply it to health and, by extension, to hair, skin and body changes they want to understand or reverse.
card.aka: GNM, German New Medicine, New Medicine, Neue Medizin, Hamer's system
card.note: Medical bodies warn that following GNM in place of conventional treatment has been linked to preventable deaths.

quick.overview:
Germanic New Medicine (GNM) is a framework devised by the German physician Ryke Geerd Hamer (1935-2017). It holds that diseases begin with a sudden shocking emotional conflict, that this leaves a mark in the brain, and that symptoms are meaningful biological programs rather than malfunctions. Followers apply this reading to the body broadly, including skin, hair and body changes, and seek to resolve the supposed conflict rather than treat the symptom.

Believers say it gives a coherent account of why illness happens and a way to understand their own symptoms. Medical organisations, including the German Cancer Society and the Swiss Cancer League, reject its claims, and authorities in several countries have taken action over deaths of patients who relied on it.
quick.how: Practitioners and followers in general terms take a history of the shock that preceded a symptom, look for a matching conflict, and describe the illness in terms of an active phase and a healing phase. GNM is taught through Hamer's books and videos and through self-published materials and online groups, and it advises against many conventional treatments such as chemotherapy and morphine.
quick.risks: The main documented harm is delay or refusal of effective treatment. Hamer's licence was revoked in 1986, he served prison time in Germany and France, and Spanish authorities held him responsible for dozens of preventable deaths. In the 1995 Olivia Pilhar case in Austria, a court ordered conventional treatment for a child with a Wilms tumour, who then recovered. Anyone with a medical concern is advised by health agencies to consult a licensed doctor.

lead: Germanic New Medicine (GNM) is a system of beliefs about disease created by Ryke Geerd Hamer, a German physician who was born in 1935 and died in 2017. It proposes that serious illness is triggered by a sudden, isolating emotional shock and that symptoms follow fixed biological laws.[1] In appearance-focused communities it surfaces as a fringe explanation for changes people want to reverse, such as hair loss, skin conditions or body changes, which GNM followers interpret as the body's meaningful response to an unresolved conflict.

Wikipedia describes the foundation story: after Hamer's son Dirk was shot in 1978 and died, Hamer developed testicular cancer and came to believe the two events were linked.[1] He named five 'biological laws', including an 'iron rule' that every disease begins with a conflict shock, a two-phase course of disease, and a claim that microbes are helpers in healing rather than causes.[1]

Medical authorities strongly disagree. The Swiss Cancer League has said no cure has been published and that the approach is dangerous because it gives patients false security; the German Cancer Research Center, the German Cancer Society and the German Medical Association reject Hamer's theories, according to Wikipedia.[1]

chain: Symptom (for example hair or skin change) is traced to a past emotional shock
Follower looks to resolve the supposed conflict instead of treating the symptom
Claimed result: the body completes its healing phase and the change reverses
angle.text: Followers treat appearance changes as signs of an underlying conflict program and try to address the emotional cause. This is a belief-based reading; no clinical results for appearance outcomes are documented.

infobox: Developed after 1978 events in Hamer's life; later formalised as five biological laws[1]
Disease starts with a conflict shock; microbes are not causes[1]
Rejected by cancer societies and medical associations[1]

paras: GNM presents itself as a complete system in which every disease is part of an evolutionary 'meaningful program'. According to Wikipedia's summary of Hamer's writings, the five laws are the iron rule of the conflict shock, a two-phase course (active conflict then healing), an ontogenetic system linking disease to embryonic germ layers and brain regions, a reinterpretation of microbes as helpers, and a 'quintessence' describing disease phases as evolved programs for emergencies.[1] Hamer claimed that a 'Hamer focus' visible on brain CT scans corresponded to the body location of the illness; radiologists identify these features as common CT ring artifacts.[1]
He published several books between 1998 and 2005, mostly through the Amici di Dirk association.[1]

Hamer studied medicine and theology at Tübingen, was licensed in 1963 and qualified in internal medicine in 1972.[1] A court revoked his licence in 1986 and reaffirmed the ruling in 2003; his habilitation thesis on GNM was rejected by Tübingen in 1986.[1] By 1997 he owned clinics in several European countries, spent time in prison in Germany (1997-1998) and France (2004-2006), and lived in Spain until 2007 and then in Norway.[1]

No studies found. A 2023 narrative review of alternative medicine in uro-oncology in the journal Urologie compiled evidence on several alternative approaches used by cancer patients, but it is a general review of other therapies and not a study of GNM.[2]

In 1995 six-year-old Olivia Pilhar in Austria, who had a Wilms tumour, was taken to Hamer by her parents; they refused conventional treatment, authorities removed custody rights, and a court later ordered conventional treatment. According to Wikipedia she recovered and was alive in 2010, and her parents received a suspended sentence.[1] Spanish authorities held Hamer responsible for dozens of preventable deaths in 2007, and press reports describe many harmed patients across Europe.[1]

Authorities in Germany and the EU have warned of the risks, and in some countries following his methods instead of effective treatment can be prosecuted as malpractice.[1] Wikipedia also documents conspiracy claims Hamer made, including antisemitic ones, which are cited as a reason for official concern.[1]

timeline.event: Ryke Geerd Hamer born in Mettmann, Germany.[1]
Hamer's son Dirk is shot and later dies; Hamer later develops cancer and begins formulating GNM.[1]
Hamer's medical licence revoked and his habilitation thesis rejected.[1]
Hamer jailed in Germany for about a year.[1]
Spanish authorities hold him responsible for dozens of preventable deaths.[1]
